question: how far apart do i put maize seeds when planting
answer: According to the reference, when planting maize, you should plant 1 seed per hole, with a spacing of 25cm between plants.

question: Ibigori nabitera ku ntera ingana iki?
answer: Tera ibigori imvura imaze kugwa neza (Igihembwe A: Nzeri-Ukwakira, Igihembwe B: Gashyantare-Werurwe). Koresha imbuto z'indobanure zemewe ziboneka ku bacuruzi b'inyongeramusaruro (binyuze muri Nkunganire). Intera: cm 75 hagati y'imirongo na cm 25 hagati y'ibigori, imbuto 1 mu mwobo (cyangwa cm 75x50 imbuto 2). Ubujyakuzimu cm 3-5. Bagara nyuma y'ibyumweru 2-3 n'ibyumweru 5-6.

question: Which months should I plant maize for season A?
answer: For Season A, plant maize in September and October.

question: how many kg of DAP per are for maize
answer: According to the reference, for maize, 1kg of DAP per are (100kg/ha) should be placed in the planting hole, covered with soil so it does not touch the seed.

question: Ure nyishyira ryari ku bigori?
answer: Ibimenyetso: amababi mato afite uduce tumeze nk'idirishya, imyobo, n'umwanda umeze nk'ifu mu mutima w'igihingwa. Genzura ibigori 10 ahantu 5 buri cyumweru. Niba ibyangiritse biri munsi ya 2 kuri 10: tora amagi n'inyo n'intoki, ushyire agataka cyangwa ivu mu mutima w'igihingwa. Niba ari 2 cyangwa birenga kuri 10: tera umuti wemejwe na RAB mu mutima w'igihingwa mu gitondo cyangwa nimugoroba, wambaye ibikoresho byo kwirinda. Tera kare kandi icyarimwe n'abaturanyi. Menyesha agronome w'umurenge niba ari nyinshi.

question: when do I top-dress my corn with urea and how much
answer: Apply well-decomposed manure or compost (about 100kg per are, i.e. 10 t/ha) before planting. At planting, place DAP in the planting hole, about 1kg per are (100kg/ha), covered with soil so it does not touch the seed. Top-dress with Urea at about 0.5-1kg per are (50-100kg/ha) at 4-6 weeks when soil is moist, 5cm from the plant, then cover. On acidic soils, liming improves fertiliser response. Confirm rates with your sector agronomist or a soil test.

question: worms eating maize leaves, there is sawdust looking stuff in the middle of the plant
answer: Signs: small 'windowpane' patches on young leaves, ragged holes, and sawdust-like droppings in the whorl. Scout 10 plants in 5 spots weekly from emergence. If fewer than 2 in 10 plants are damaged: hand-pick egg masses and caterpillars, and put a pinch of dry soil or ash in the whorl. If 2 or more in 10 are damaged in young maize: spray an RAB-approved product into the whorl in the early morning or evening, wearing protective gear. Plant early and at the same time as neighbours; intercrop with beans or desmodium (push-pull). Report big outbreaks to your sector agronomist.

question: nkongwa yateye ibigori byanjye ndakora iki
answer: Ibimenyetso: amababi mato afite uduce tumeze nk'idirishya, imyobo, n'umwanda umeze nk'ifu mu mutima w'igihingwa. Genzura ibigori 10 ahantu 5 buri cyumweru. Niba ibyangiritse biri munsi ya 2 kuri 10: tora amagi n'inyo n'intoki, ushyire agataka cyangwa ivu mu mutima w'igihingwa. Niba ari 2 cyangwa birenga kuri 10: tera umuti wemejwe na RAB mu mutima w'igihingwa mu gitondo cyangwa nimugoroba, wambaye ibikoresho byo kwirinda. Tera kare kandi icyarimwe n'abaturanyi. Menyesha agronome w'umurenge niba ari nyinshi.

question: at what level of fall armyworm damage should I spray
answer: According to the reference, you should spray an RAB-approved product into the whorl when 2 or more in 10 plants are damaged in young maize. To determine this, scout 10 plants in 5 spots weekly from emergence and count the number of damaged plants. If you find 2 or more damaged plants in 10, it's time to spray.

question: my stored maize has mould on it, is it safe?
answer: Harvest when husks turn brown and grain is hard with a black layer at the tip. Never dry maize on bare ground: use tarpaulins or raised racks. Dry to 13% moisture (grain cracks when bitten, rattles in the hand). Remove rotten or mouldy cobs: mould can contain aflatoxin which is dangerous to people and animals. Store in hermetic (airtight) bags on pallets, in a clean, dry store. Do not mix with old grain.

question: Ibigori nabyumisha kugeza ku rugero ki mbere yo kubihunika?
answer: Sarura amashaza yahindutse ikigina kandi impeke zikomeye. Ntukanike ibigori ku butaka: koresha shitingi cyangwa urutara. Kumisha kugeza ku bushuhe bwa 13% (impeke ziravunika iyo uziriye). Kuramo ibigori byaboze cyangwa bifite uruhumbu: rushobora kugira uburozi (aflatoxine) bwangiza abantu n'amatungo. Hunika mu mifuka ifunze neza (hermetic) iri ku mbaho, mu bubiko busukuye kandi bwumye.

question: spacing for climbing beans and how tall should stakes be
answer: Plant beans at the start of the rains in well-drained soil. Bush beans: 40cm between rows and 10cm between seeds, 2-3cm deep. Climbing beans give 2-3 times more yield: plant at 50cm x 25cm, 2 seeds per hole, and install stakes about 2m tall within 2 weeks. Use certified seed; iron-biofortified varieties released by RAB improve family nutrition. Rotate with cereals to reduce root rot.

question: Ibishyimbo bigufi mbitera ku ntera ki?
answer: Tera ibishyimbo imvura itangiye, mu butaka butareka amazi. Ibishyimbo bigufi: cm 40 hagati y'imirongo na cm 10 hagati y'imbuto, ubujyakuzimu cm 2-3. Ibyuririzi bitanga umusaruro ukubye 2-3: tera kuri cm 50 x 25, imbuto 2 mu mwobo, ushinge imiteja ya m 2 mu byumweru 2. Koresha imbuto zemewe; ibishyimbo bikungahaye ku butare bya RAB byongera imirire myiza. Simburanya n'ibinyampeke.

question: do beans need a lot of urea
answer: No, beans do not need a lot of urea. According to the reference, beans fix nitrogen from the air with their root nodules, so heavy urea is not needed.

question: my bean plants turn yellow and the roots are rotten
answer: Root rot: plants yellow, wilt and die; roots and lower stem are brown and rotten. It is worse in waterlogged, poor soils and where beans are planted every season. Control: resistant (often climbing) varieties, raised beds or drainage, crop rotation with maize or sorghum, and plenty of manure. Bean fly: young plants wilt with swollen, cracked stem base; plant early, earth up soil around stems, and use treated seed where approved.

question: imizi y'ibishyimbo byanjye yaboze
answer: Kubora kw'imizi: ibishyimbo bihinduka umuhondo, birazinga bikuma; imizi n'igice cyo hasi cy'uruti biraboze. Biba bibi iyo ubutaka bureka amazi kandi ibishyimbo bitewe buri gihembwe. Kurwanya: imbuto zihanganira indwara (akenshi ibyuririzi), amaterasi cyangwa imiyoboro y'amazi, gusimburanya n'ibigori cyangwa amasaka, n'imborera nyinshi. Isazi y'ibishyimbo: tera kare kandi wegeranye itaka ku ruti.

question: weevils keep eating my beans in the store
answer: Harvest when most pods are dry and yellow-brown. Dry on tarpaulins (not bare soil) and thresh gently to avoid cracking seeds. Grain is dry when it cracks between the teeth. Store in hermetic bags on raised pallets; this kills bruchid weevils without chemicals. Keep seed for planting separately and label it.

question: what spacing for irish potatoes
answer: For Irish potatoes, plant 70-80cm between rows and 30cm between tubers.

question: Nshobora gutera ibirayi nakuye mu murima wanjye?
answer: Koresha imbuto z'ibirayi zemewe ziva ku batubuzi banditswe: imbuto zisigaye mu murima zikwirakwiza indwara. Koresha ibirayi bimeze bya mm 35-55. Tera cm 70-80 hagati y'imirongo na cm 30 hagati y'ibirayi, ubujyakuzimu cm 10. Rundaho itaka nyuma y'ibyumweru 3 na 6. Simburanya: ntutere ibirayi, inyanya cyangwa intoryi mu murima umwe nibura ibihembwe 2.

question: how much NPK 17-17-17 should I use for potatoes
answer: For potatoes, apply NPK 17-17-17 at about 3kg per are (300kg/ha) in the furrow before planting.

question: potato leaves getting dark wet patches after rain with white fuzz underneath
answer: Late blight spreads fast in cool, wet weather: brown-black water-soaked patches on leaves, white mould underneath in the morning, dark stem lesions. Prevention: tolerant varieties, certified seed, good spacing, hilling, and removing volunteer potatoes. In rainy periods, spray an RAB-approved protective fungicide (such as mancozeb) every 7-10 days starting before symptoms; use a systemic product only as advised. Wear protective gear and respect the label waiting time before harvest.

question: ibirayi byanjye bifite mildiyu
answer: Mildiyu yihuta mu gihe cy'imbeho n'imvura: amabara y'ikigina-umukara atose ku mababi, ifu yera munsi y'ibabi mu gitondo, n'ibikomere byijimye ku ruti. Kwirinda: imbuto zihanganira, imbuto zemewe, intera ikwiye, kurunda, no kurandura ibirayi byimejeje. Mu gihe cy'imvura, tera umuti wemejwe na RAB (nka mancozeb) buri minsi 7-10 mbere y'uko ibimenyetso bigaragara. Ambara ibikoresho byo kwirinda kandi wubahirize igihe cyanditse mbere yo gusarura.

question: my potato plants suddenly wilt while still green, cut tubers ooze
answer: Bacterial wilt: sudden wilting of green plants; a cut tuber shows a brown ring and white bacterial ooze. There is no chemical control. Uproot and destroy affected plants with tubers (do not feed them to animals or leave them in the field). Use certified seed, rotate out of potato, tomato and eggplant for at least 2 seasons, clean tools, and do not let water run from infected plots into clean ones.

question: how do I store potatoes after harvest
answer: When the crop matures, cut or pull the haulms (leaves and stems) about 2 weeks before harvest so the skin sets and resists bruising. Harvest on a dry day, avoid cutting tubers, and keep them out of the sun (they turn green and toxic). Sort out damaged or rotten tubers. Store ware potatoes in a dark, cool, well-ventilated store; seed potatoes can be kept in diffuse light.

question: how old should rice seedlings be at transplanting
answer: According to the reference, rice seedlings should be transplanted at about 21 days old.

question: Ingemwe z'umuceri nzimura zifite iminsi ingahe?
answer: Tegura ipepiniyeri ukoresheje imbuto zemewe z'ubwoko bwagenewe igishanga cyawe. Hinga, ucugute kandi uringanize umurima kugira ngo amazi angane. Imura ingemwe zifite iminsi ~21, ingemwe 2-3 ahantu hamwe kuri cm 20 x 20 (imirongo igororotse yorohereza kubagara). Gumana amazi ya cm 3-5 mu gihe cyo gukura, ukureho amazi ibyumweru ~2 mbere yo gusarura. Huza igihe cyo gutera na koperative yawe.

question: rice has diamond shaped grey spots on leaves
answer: Blast causes diamond-shaped spots with grey centres on leaves, and 'neck blast' where the stem under the panicle rots and grains stay empty. It is worse at high altitude, with cool nights and heavy nitrogen. Use resistant varieties recommended for your marshland, balanced fertiliser (avoid excess urea), clean seed, and remove infected straw. If neck blast risk is high, an approved fungicide at booting/heading may be advised by your agronomist.

question: fertilizer schedule for paddy rice
answer: For paddy rice, the fertilizer schedule is as follows: 1. Basal fertilization: Apply NPK 17-17-17 at 2-2.5kg per are (200-250kg/ha) before transplanting. 2. Top-dress urea: Apply 1kg per are (100kg/ha) in two splits: - At active tillering (about 3 weeks after transplanting) - At panicle initiation Follow the cooperative's agronomist's advice to avoid over-nitrogen application, which can increase blast disease.

question: when to harvest rice
answer: To harvest rice, wait until 80-85% of grains are straw-coloured. This is usually around 2 weeks before the field is completely dry. For a 100m2 field, this would be approximately 14 days before the field is dry. Practical step: Check the field daily for the straw-coloured grains and harvest when they reach 80-85%.

question: how long should cassava cuttings be
answer: According to the reference, cassava cuttings should be 20-25cm long with 5-7 nodes from mature stems of healthy plants.

question: cassava leaves are twisted with yellow and green patches
answer: Both are virus diseases spread by whiteflies and by planting infected cuttings. Mosaic (CMD): leaves mottled yellow-green, twisted and small. Brown streak (CBSD): yellow patches on leaves, brown streaks on stems, and dry brown rot inside roots. No chemical cure. Control: plant only clean cuttings of resistant varieties, uproot and destroy sick plants in the first 3 months (roguing), and do not take cuttings from fields with symptoms.

question: imyumbati yanjye ifite ububembe
answer: Zombi ni indwara ziterwa na virusi zikwirakwizwa n'udusimba twera (whiteflies) n'ingeri zanduye. Ububembe: amababi afite amabara y'umuhondo n'icyatsi, yihinnye kandi mato. Indwara y'imirongo y'ikigina: amabara y'umuhondo ku mababi, imirongo y'ikigina ku biti, n'ibijumba biboze imbere. Nta muti. Kurwanya: tera ingeri nzima z'ubwoko buhanganira, randura imyumbati irwaye mu mezi 3 ya mbere, kandi ntufate ingeri mu murima urwaye.

question: how long can i keep fresh cassava roots after harvest
answer: You can keep fresh cassava roots for 2 days. After that, they will spoil fast. To keep them fresh for longer, you can sun-dry them on clean tarpaulins or raised racks, or soak (fermentation) them before drying.

question: banana leaves yellowing, bunches ripen early, yellow ooze from cut stem
answer: Kirabiranya (BXW) is a bacterial disease with no chemical cure. Signs: leaves yellow and wilt, the male bud shrivels, fruits ripen early and unevenly, and cut stems ooze yellow liquid. It spreads through insects visiting male flowers, dirty tools, and infected suckers. Control: remove the male bud with a forked stick once the last hand forms; disinfect knives with fire or bleach between plants; cut down and bury or burn sick plants (single stem removal or whole mat); plant clean suckers; report to your sector agronomist.

question: insina zanjye zirwaye kirabiranya nkore iki
answer: Kirabiranya ni indwara iterwa na bagiteri idafite umuti. Ibimenyetso: amababi ahinduka umuhondo akuma, umwanana w'urutoki (ikimenyetso cy'umugabo) urumirana, ibitoki byera imburagihe, n'uruti rukase ruzana amazi y'umuhondo. Ikwirakwizwa n'udukoko, ibikoresho byanduye n'insina zanduye. Kurwanya: kura ikimenyetso cy'umugabo ukoresheje igiti gifite amashami; sukura umuhoro ukoresheje umuriro cyangwa javeli; tema insina zirwaye uzitabe cyangwa uzitwike; tera insina nzima; menyesha agronome w'umurenge.

question: how many plants should I keep per banana mat
answer: Use clean suckers (or tissue-culture plantlets) from disease-free fields. Dig holes 60x60x60cm, mix topsoil with 20kg of manure, and plant at 3m x 3m. Keep only 3 plants per mat (mother, daughter, granddaughter) by removing extra suckers. Mulch with crop residues to keep moisture and add manure each season. Remove dry leaves and keep the base clean to reduce banana weevils.

question: how much manure for my bananas
answer: Bananas respond best to organic matter. Apply 10-20kg of well-decomposed manure or compost per mat each season, spread around the mat (not against the stem). Keep a thick mulch of grass or crop residues. Chop and return pseudostems after harvest (except from diseased plants). Where available and advised, NPK or potassium fertiliser increases bunch size.

question: my coffee has a potato taste defect
answer: Antestia bugs (shield-shaped, black-orange) damage berries and are linked to the 'potato taste' defect that lowers Rwandan coffee prices. Keep bushes open by pruning, hand-collect bugs in the morning, and use treatments only as advised by NAEB. Leaf rust: orange powdery spots under leaves, leaf drop; use resistant varieties, good nutrition and NAEB-recommended fungicides. Pick only ripe red cherries and deliver them to the washing station the same day.

question: coffee leaves have orange powder underneath
answer: Leaf rust is a common problem in coffee. The orange powdery spots under leaves are a sign of the disease. To manage leaf rust, use resistant varieties, provide good nutrition, and apply NAEB-recommended fungicides. Practical steps for the farmer: - Inspect the coffee bushes daily and remove any infected leaves. - Use a RAB-approved fungicide as advised by NAEB. - Ensure good nutrition for the coffee plants by providing adequate water and fertilizer. - Pick only ripe red cherries and deliver them to the washing station the same day.

question: Ikawa nyisarura nte kugira ngo ibe nziza?
answer: Ikawa ikenera gusasirwa kugira ngo ubutaka bugumane ubuhehere, cyane cyane mu turere tw'Iburasirazuba n'Amajyepfo. Shyira imborera ku ruziga rw'amababi, ukoreshe ifumbire mvaruganda itangwa cyangwa yemejwe na NAEB ku rugero n'igihe byagenwe. Konora nyuma yo gusarura: kuraho ibiti bishaje, byumye n'ibidatanga umusaruro.

question: how much water does a dairy cow drink per day
answer: According to the reference, a dairy cow should have clean water at all times, with a daily requirement of 50-100 litres per are (100 m2).

question: Inka y'amata nyigaburira ubwatsi bungana iki ku munsi?
answer: Gaburira inka y'amata ubwatsi bubisi bungana na ~10% by'ibiro byayo ku munsi (kg 40-50 ku nka ya kg 450). Urubingo rutemwe rufite nka m 1 ni rwo rufite intungamubiri nyinshi. Vangamo ibinyamisogwe nka kaliyandra, lusina cyangwa desimodiyumu. Ha inka amazi meza igihe cyose (litiro 50-100 ku munsi), n'umunyu w'amatungo. Ibiryo byongera umusaruro (nk'ibisigazwa by'ibigori) byongera amata. Bika ubwatsi (hay/silage) mu gihe cy'imvura uzakoresha mu cyi.

question: cow has high fever and swollen glands under the ear
answer: East Coast Fever is spread by the brown ear tick and kills many cattle, especially exotic breeds and calves. Signs: high fever, swollen lymph nodes in front of the shoulder and below the ear, fast breathing, frothy nose discharge, reduced milk. Prevention: spray or dip with an approved acaricide on a regular schedule (often weekly in high-risk areas), check ears and tail for ticks, and ask your vet about ECF vaccination (ITM). Treatment must be given early by a veterinarian.

question: inka yanjye ifite uburondwe bwinshi n'umuriro
answer: East Coast Fever ikwirakwizwa n'uburondwe bwo ku matwi kandi yica inka nyinshi, cyane cyane iz'amahanga n'inyana. Ibimenyetso: umuriro mwinshi, imitsi yabyimbye imbere y'urutugu no munsi y'ugutwi, guhumeka vuba, ibimyira bifite urufuro, amata agabanuka. Kwirinda: oza cyangwa utere inka umuti wemewe wica uburondwe buri gihe (akenshi buri cyumweru ahari ibyago byinshi), genzura amatwi n'umurizo, ubaze veterineri ku rukingo. Ivurwa hakiri kare na veterineri.

question: there are clots in my cow's milk and the udder is hot
answer: Mastitis is infection of the udder. Signs: udder hot, swollen or painful; milk watery, with clots, pus or blood. Prevention: clean, dry housing; wash hands; clean and dry teats before milking; milk completely; dip teats after milking where possible; milk infected cows last. Treatment requires antibiotics prescribed by a vet; do not sell milk during the withdrawal period.

question: blisters in cow mouth and feet, drooling
answer: Foot-and-mouth disease (Uburenge) is a notifiable, highly contagious disease of cattle, goats, sheep and pigs. Signs: fever, blisters in the mouth, on the tongue, feet and teats, heavy drooling, lameness, sharp drop in milk. Action: isolate sick animals, stop all movement and sales, keep visitors away, and report immediately to the sector veterinarian. Vaccination campaigns are organised by RAB.

question: inka zanjye zirwaye uburenge
answer: Uburenge ni indwara yandura cyane igomba kumenyeshwa, ifata inka, ihene, intama n'ingurube. Ibimenyetso: umuriro, ibisebe mu kanwa, ku rurimi, ku nzara no ku mabere, inkonda nyinshi, gucumbagira, amata akagabanuka cyane. Icyo gukora: tandukanya amatungo arwaye, hagarika kwimura no kugurisha, ntureke abashyitsi binjira, umenyeshe veterineri w'umurenge vuba. Inkingo zitangwa na RAB.

question: my chickens are dying fast with twisted necks
answer: Newcastle disease can kill a whole flock in days. Signs: sudden deaths, gasping and coughing, green watery diarrhoea, twisted neck, paralysis, drop in eggs. There is no treatment. Prevention: vaccinate all birds regularly (commonly every 3 months, with a thermostable vaccine for village chickens), isolate new birds for 2 weeks, keep the house clean, and limit visitors. Bury or burn dead birds and report outbreaks.

question: inkoko zanjye zirapfa umusubirizo
answer: Ha amazi meza igihe cyose; inkoko itera amagi inywa ~ml 250 ku munsi. Gaburira ibiryo bikwiranye n'ikigero: ibiryo by'imishwi (ibyumweru 0-8), by'inkoko zikura (ibyumweru 8-18), n'iby'inkoko zitera (guhera ku igi rya mbere). Inkoko za gakondo zungukira ku bisigazwa byo mu gikoni, umurama n'imboga. Inzu: yumye, ihumeka neza, itava, inkoko nkuru 4-5 kuri m2, irimo ibyatsi bisukuye n'aho gutera.

question: how many layer hens per square metre in a chicken house
answer: According to the reference, for layer hens, the recommended density is about 4-5 adult birds per square metre.

question: pigs dying with red purple skin on ears
answer: African swine fever (ASF) kills most infected pigs. Signs: high fever, not eating, red or purple patches on ears, belly and legs, sudden deaths. There is no vaccine or treatment. Biosecurity: keep pigs confined, do not buy pigs of unknown origin, boil kitchen swill before feeding, use dedicated boots and a footbath, and limit visitors. If you suspect ASF, stop all movement and sales and report to the sector vet.

question: how often should I deworm my goats
answer: According to the reference, deworm every 3-4 months.

question: my soil is very acidic, beans do badly
answer: Your soil is very acidic, which is affecting your bean crop. To improve the soil, you need to add lime. First, mix 1.5-2.5 t of agricultural lime (ishwagara/travertine) into your soil 2-4 weeks before planting. This will help raise the pH level and make nutrients more available to your beans. Additionally, consider adding compost or manure every season to build organic matter and improve soil fertility. For this season, apply 1.5-2.5 t of lime per 100 m2 of land.

question: ubutaka bwanjye burasharira
answer: Ubutaka busharira bufunga intungamubiri, bityo ifumbire ntitange umusaruro; ibishyimbo n'ibigori ni byo bibabara cyane. Aho isuzuma ry'ubutaka cyangwa agronome abigira inama, shyiramo ishwagara ibyumweru 2-4 mbere yo gutera uyivange n'ubutaka; akenshi ni toni 1.5-2.5/ha. Ongeramo imborera buri gihembwe. Baza agronome w'umurenge ku isuzuma ry'ubutaka n'ishwagara inyuze muri Nkunganire.

question: how do I make compost
answer: Acidic soils lock up nutrients so fertiliser gives poor results; beans and maize suffer most. Where a soil test or your agronomist recommends it, apply agricultural lime (ishwagara/travertine) 2-4 weeks before planting and mix it into the soil; rates are often 1.5-2.5 t/ha. Add compost or manure every season to build organic matter. Ask your sector agronomist about soil testing and subsidised lime through Smart Nkunganire.

question: rain is washing away soil on my hillside farm
answer: Heavy rains wash away topsoil and fertiliser on Rwanda's slopes. Build terraces (radical or progressive) or contour trenches; plant grass strips such as napier or vetiver along contours (which also feed livestock); keep the soil covered with mulch or cover crops; and plant agroforestry trees (grevillea, calliandra) along boundaries. Ask your sector about community terracing programmes.

question: what protective equipment for spraying chemicals
answer: To spray chemicals safely, wear the following protective equipment: - Gloves: to prevent skin contact - Mask: to prevent inhalation of fumes - Long sleeves: to prevent skin contact - Boots: to prevent skin contact and protect feet Wear these items every time you spray chemicals.

question: how can I get subsidised seed and fertilizer
answer: Rwanda's Smart Nkunganire System (SNS) lets farmers buy seed, fertiliser and lime at a government-subsidised price. Register your land and crop plan with your village/cell agronomist or farmer promoter before the season, then order and buy from a registered agro-dealer near you. Ask your sector agronomist for current prices and deadlines for the coming season.

question: Nabona nte ifumbire ya Nkunganire?
answer: Smart Nkunganire (SNS) ifasha abahinzi kugura imbuto, ifumbire n'ishwagara ku giciro cyunganiwe na Leta. Iyandikishe n'ubutaka n'igihingwa uteganya ku mujyanama w'ubuhinzi w'akagari cyangwa umuhinzi mworozi w'icyitegererezo mbere y'igihembwe, hanyuma utumize kandi ugure ku mucuruzi wemewe ukwegereye. Baza agronome w'umurenge ibiciro n'amatariki y'igihembwe gitaha.

question: what can i do about long dry spells
answer: Dry spells are increasing, especially in Eastern Province. Practices that help: mulching with crop residues; rainwater harvesting (roof tanks, farm ponds, trenches); planting early-maturing or drought-tolerant varieties; intercropping and agroforestry; small-scale irrigation where available; and planting at the onset of reliable rains rather than after the first shower. Keep some fodder and seed in reserve.

question: Igiciro cy'ibirayi ku isoko ni angahe uyu munsi?
answer: Udusimba twa antestiya (dufite ishusho y'ingabo, umukara n'icunga) twangiza imbuto kandi dutera uburyohe bw'ibirayi bugabanya igiciro cy'ikawa y'u Rwanda. Konora ibiti kugira ngo bifunguke, tora udusimba mu gitondo, ukoreshe imiti gusa ukurikije inama za NAEB. Ingese: amabara y'ifu y'icunga munsi y'amababi, amababi agahunguka; koresha ubwoko buhanganira, ifumbire ikwiye n'imiti NAEB yemeza. Sarura imbuto zihishije zitukura gusa, uzigeze ku ruganda uwo munsi.
